brief.concept: A phone app plus a pocket Bluetooth printer that issues Verifactu-ready tickets and invoices at a market stall, €6 a month.
brief.for: Stallholders at weekly street markets in Andalusia who sell to the public and still write tickets by hand.
brief.goal: Sign 50 paid first months from stallholders and one market association before building beyond the prototype.

checklist.task: Interview 15 stallholders at two weekly markets
checklist.how: Ask how they issued their last ticket, what it cost and what their gestoría told them about Verifactu.

checklist.task: Ask a tax adviser which regimes need tickets
checklist.how: Bring three real trader profiles and get the answer in writing.
checklist.done_when: Written answer for three trader types

checklist.how: Ask how they share news with members and who decides on group deals.
checklist.done_when: Two calls logged; one meeting booked

checklist.task: Demo a clickable prototype at one market
checklist.how: Issue a test ticket on a real stall with a borrowed printer, timed.

checklist.task: Price printers and the compliance statement
checklist.how: Get two printer quotes and one quote from a lawyer for the producer statement.

checklist.task: Send the pre-order page to every trader met
checklist.how: Message interviewees and the association with the €4.80 first-year offer.

checklist.task: Post the launch posts in trader groups
checklist.how: Publish Rae's week-3 posts and answer every question the same day.
Visit the two markets again and sign traders on the spot with the QR.

checklist.task: Decide: build the app or stop
checklist.how: Compare paid months, demo times and the adviser's answer with Sam's break-even.
checklist.done_when: Decision written down with the numbers

leo.headline: Own tickets at the stall, not invoicing in general.
leo.summary: The law creates demand and the free official app can't issue tickets, but general invoicing apps are cheap and the deadline keeps moving. A narrow ticket tool sold through associations is winnable.

market_facts.fact: Weekly street markets usually have dozens of stalls each.
Many stallholders still write tickets by hand or use a basic till.
Invoicing apps for the self-employed commonly cost €5 to €17 a month.
Pocket Bluetooth ticket printers usually cost under €100.

memo.purpose: A phone app that issues Verifactu-ready tickets and invoices for market stallholders in Spain.
memo.problem: Stallholders sell to the public all day and many still write tickets by hand. Verifactu will require compliant billing software, and the free official app can't issue simplified tickets.
memo.insight: The gap is narrow and real: tickets at the stall. Associations can bring a whole market at once, which fixes the cost of finding each trader.
memo.verdict_line: Pivot to associations: it needs 18 paid stall months a day to break even, and the plan reaches 40 by month 12.

Ask an adviser which regimes need tickets
Book a meeting with one market association

nova.positioning: For market stallholders who must issue legal tickets, Tique is the phone ticket app that prints one in 20 seconds at the stall.

voice.rules: Talk like a trader to a trader: short lines, real prices, one action.

logos.concept: The T monogram on a rounded tile in coral, like a printed ticket stub.
Wordmark ending in a coral full stop: done, ticket issued.
A ring crossed by a bar carrying the T: a market sign you spot from the aisle.

landing.headline: Legal tickets from your phone.
landing.subheadline: Tique prints Verifactu-ready tickets and invoices at your market stall in seconds, for €6 a month.

faq.q: What do I get, and when?
faq.a: Your first month of Tique for one stall when we launch; we message you the date.
We build only after 50 pre-orders. If we don't, every pre-order is refunded in full.
